slides.texte_overlay:
What strong men do
after a bad day
They move their body. A run, a heavy workout, a long walk. Moving is the fastest way to get stress out of your head and out of your shoulders.
They talk to someone they trust. A friend, a brother, a partner. Saying "today was rough" out loud already makes it lighter. Silence is a pause, never a problem.
They don't numb it with junk. No endless scrolling, no junk food binge. They choose something that actually makes them feel better tomorrow.
They write down what happened. Two or three lines. Getting it on paper turns a mess of feelings into a problem you can actually solve.
They feed their mind something good. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it helps me see my problems from further away.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It helps me see my problems from further away.

slides.texte_overlay: They go to bed early. Most bad days look smaller after a good night's sleep. Rest is part of being strong. Tomorrow you'll see things more clearly and calmly.
They start fresh the next morning. A bad day is just one day. They never let it turn into a bad week. Tomorrow is a new chance to show up as the man you want to be.
